title: Modeling Human Subjectivity in LLMs Using Explicit and Implicit Human Factors in Personas

bias_targets.methodology: Correlating subjective annotation ratings (toxicity and stigma) and n-gram frequencies in text generated about the Israel/Palestine conflict with explicit age descriptions or age-associated names in the LLM prompts.
Correlating subjective annotation ratings and n-gram frequencies in text generated about parenting with explicit gender descriptions or gender-associated names in the LLM prompts.
Correlating subjective annotation ratings and n-gram frequencies in text generated about immigration with explicit political ideology prompts (e.g., conservative vs. liberal).
Correlating subjective annotation ratings and n-gram frequencies in text generated about policing with explicit race descriptions (Black/White) or race-associated names in the LLM prompts.

Correlating subjective annotation ratings for stigma and n-gram frequencies in text generated about marijuana legalization with explicit prompts indicating a persona's lived experience with substance use.
